summary: The discussion proposes a new Parquet logical type, WIRE, that stores serialized wire-format messages (e.g., protobuf) as opaque bytes while allowing selected fields to be shredded into columnar form for efficient querying. The results highlight that gains shrink when measured against highly optimized existing code and that adopting a new layout adds complexity to writers. The discussion centers on creating a higher‑level document that compares several numeric encodings—DELTA_BINARY_PACKED, PFOR, FastLanes, and potential optimizations—across speed, storage efficiency, and development effort. Antoine apologizes for earlier harsh remarks and emphasizes the importance of evaluating maintenance effort to move ideas into production.
